source.interpretation: Simulation star-family particles, not observed individual stars. Source masses are unchanged; no ages, populations, luminosities or dust are inferred.

transform.method: Recover raw simulation coordinates; subtract the measured MW star median; apply an active +3.916781113 degree Z rotation derived to reproduce the paper's rounded Table 2 LMC position; subtract the paper's Sun position; convert Galactic Cartesian to ICRS; transform into the existing object-local frame.
transform.limitation: The paper specifies MW centering and rotation to the observed LMC angle but does not publish the exact angle or center estimator. The MW star median and +3.916781113 degree rotation are a derived diagnostic that reproduces its rounded Table 2 positions; this is not observational astrometry.
transform.interpretation: One observer-relative affine maps raw simulation Cartesian positions into the existing Sun-ICRF object frame.

limitations: The paper specifies MW centering and rotation to the observed LMC angle but does not publish the exact angle or center estimator. The MW star median and +3.916781113 degree rotation are a derived diagnostic that reproduces its rounded Table 2 positions; this is not observational astrometry.
This is a bounded-resolution overview of simulated stellar mass, not a new high-resolution depth measurement.
It contains no observational photograph, gas, dust, extinction, calibrated photometry or morphology fit.

approximation.method: Filtered scalar fields; decoded after filtering; integrated RGB emission; exponential shared opacity with optical RGB ratios in ordinary alpha.
limitations: Shared-opacity display emission preserves column-constant chromaticity before RGBA8 quantization; varying chromaticity remains a slab approximation. Extinction is unsupported.
Finite slices and axis handoffs approximate a continuous field; angle-dependent opacity and sampling differences remain.
No runtime ray integration, near-field noise or global HDR display pass.
